sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *quiero salir* and *quiero que salgas* from B2 Unit 4: the choice depends on who does the second action. If the person who wants is also the person who acts, use an infinitive: *Los trabajadores quieren tener contrato*. If someone else acts, use *que* + subjunctive: *Los sindicatos quieren que las empresas paguen el salario mínimo*. Reports about work and migration are full of both.

sections.title: Same person or new person?
rows: Los migrantes quieren trabajar con contrato.
same person: the migrants want to work with a contract
Los sindicatos quieren que las empresas paguen el salario mínimo.
new person: the unions want the companies to pay the minimum wage
same person: the families hope to find work
Las organizaciones piden que el gobierno proteja los ríos.
new person: the organisations ask the government to protect the rivers

items.spanish: Muchos trabajadores migrantes quieren trabajar con un contrato legal.
items.english: Many migrant workers want to work with a legal contract.

items.spanish: Los sindicatos quieren que las empresas paguen el salario mínimo.
items.english: The unions want the companies to pay the minimum wage.

items.spanish: Las organizaciones ambientales piden que el gobierno proteja los ríos.
items.english: Environmental organisations ask the government to protect the rivers.

items.spanish: Los jóvenes de la costa esperan encontrar empleo cerca de su casa.
items.english: Young people on the coast hope to find a job near home.

sections.content: English hides the second person (*they want the companies to pay*), so ask yourself who does the second action. Same person: infinitive. New person: *que* + subjunctive. Not *quieren que tener*, and not *quieren las empresas pagar*.
